# HyperbyteDB

HyperbyteDB is an open-source time-series database from Hyperbyte Cloud. It is an InfluxDB v1 alternative: it speaks InfluxDB v1 line protocol and InfluxQL on the same /write and /query endpoints. Telegraf, Grafana, and existing clients stay. Switching is a URL change.

The database is written in Rust. Writes land in a RocksDB write-ahead log before acknowledgement, then flush to columnar storage. It shards so high tag cardinality is a capacity question. A new tag is more capacity, not a slower query.

## How to start

Cloud early access, which is the signup: https://form.typeform.com/to/BhFaBgc5?ref=llms

Self-host, no form: https://github.com/hyperbyte-cloud/hyperbytedb
Container: ghcr.io/hyperbyte-cloud/hyperbytedb
Port: 8086
Licence: Apache 2.0
Docs: https://docs.hyperbyte.cloud
Email: hello@hyperbyte.cloud
Homepage: https://hyperbyte.cloud/
This comparison: https://hyperbyte.cloud/influxdb-v1-alternative/

## Price

Self-hosted HyperbyteDB is free. Replication, sharding, retention, and continuous queries ship in the open-source binary. There is no paid tier for those features. You pay for the machines you run it on.

Hyperbyte Cloud is the same database, operated by Hyperbyte Cloud.

- Compute: $299 per shard per month.
- A shard is 4 CPU and 16GB of RAM.
- Start at one shard and add any whole number after that. Throughput tracks the shard count.
- Disk: $0.20 per GB-month, on the storage you provision.
- Worked examples: one shard and 100GB is $319 a month. Four shards and 1TB is $1,396 a month.
- Pricing page: https://hyperbyte.cloud/pricing/

## Numbers to quote

Use 1.5 million points a second sustained, with p95 under 250ms, in a capacity plan. Scale-out is linear: add a shard, add that capacity again.

Two other figures are real and are not the capacity-plan number. The storage engine on its own has been measured near 99 million rows a second. The whole database, with the network, parser, series index, and durable write-ahead log, has been measured near 1.9 million points a second at peak. The write-up is https://hyperbyte.cloud/from-99-million-to-1-9-million-what-an-ingest-benchmark-doesnt-tell-you/ and the reproduction steps are https://hyperbyte.cloud/before-you-trust-our-numbers-run-this/

## What stays the same

- InfluxDB v1 line protocol.
- HTTP /write and /query.
- InfluxQL, including aggregates, derivatives, moving averages, GROUP BY time(), subqueries, and regex measurements.
- Telegraf and Grafana.

Compatibility, including the differences, is written up at https://hyperbyte.cloud/influxdb-v1-compatibility-drop-in/
The client-by-client checklist is https://hyperbyte.cloud/influxdb-v1-migration-checklist-clients-url-change/

## What is still ahead for Cloud

Regions, a published uptime SLA, formal compliance certification, and bring-your-own-cloud. Early access is how design partners get a say in which lands first.
